versions.notes: The venue becomes a screen of its own. A new Venue tab draws the room rather than the rig: an Elements list, an Element Settings block and a stacked Top View / Elevation view, in the same shape the Sources tab uses so switching tabs does not rearrange the window. Elements come in three kinds - Listening (an audience), Structure (built scenery) and Object (a prop) - each in its own colour, and each is four free points rather than a rectangle, so a venue dragged out of square still works everywhere downstream. Everything added lands on the origin, as ArrayCalc does. The tab is wired to the solver: every Listening element becomes a listening plane on the Sources plan, which is what the prediction clips its map to and what the plane tag reports avg / min / max / spread over, with the ear height carried across. Venue owns the truth and the planes are a projection re-run on every change; annotations carry a venueIndex so the projection replaces only the rows it created, leaving a shape drawn by hand on the plan untouched. Structure and Object are deliberately not projected - a stage is where the audience is not. Elements are edited on the canvas: click to select, drag the body to move, drag a corner to move that point, drag an edge midpoint to move both its ends so a rectangle resizes rather than skews, with an even-odd crossing test rather than a bounding box. Both venue panes share one camera - the wheel zooms about the pointer and keeps the point under it pinned, a drag on empty canvas pans - so a metre stays in the same column in the plan and the elevation. Duplicate, Mirror x, Mirror y and Delete hang off the shape's own right-click menu, mirroring about the origin so a left-hand stand mirrors into the right-hand one, and venue elements are saved in the .atmk project. Consistency pass across the whole application: every plot now draws from one FigmaPlotStyle sheet - the same field, grid, frame, tick and mark colours, the same 2 m / 5 ft grid rule and the same 48 px-per-2 m opening scale - so a 10 m box is the same size on every tab and the two can no longer drift apart; x runs negative-left and positive-right on the venue panes as it does on the plan; and the Sources panel takes the Venue palette, which it had been missing by a few levels of grey at every step. Fixed: the unit toggle did nothing, through three separate breaks - the change handler refreshed the legacy sidebar rather than either of the two on screen, FieldBox captured its unit suffix once at construction so no relayout could change it, and the venue axes were hardcoded to metres; the grid step is unit-aware too, five feet in Imperial so the rules land on whole feet. "Sources" appeared twice, the view strip's left cell and the panel's own header one bar under the other. Elements drawn past the edge of a field painted over the tick labels. Venue grid rules and figures were swept about the origin rather than the camera, so panning left the far side blank and unlabelled. An axis figure whose rule sat within half a label of the frame was drawn half outside it. The Sources elevation framed the rig's bounding box, so a flown array collapsed to the 4 m floor and zoomed until the throw was off the pane. The SPL caption and the plan grid were drawn white on white with Mapping off, the canvas forced to the heatmap's black floor while the ink was chosen from the theme. Known limits: Rigging Angles lists every speaker in the scene rather than one source's cabinets, because one Speaker is one source here and there is no array-grouping layer yet - No. of Cabinets is inert for the same reason; Aud. Height stays editable on Structure and Object, where it means nothing; and ear height documents a plane without moving the prediction, since the measured data is one horizontal plane per device.

Each cabinet model is now simulated at its OWN frequency. Picking the directivity pattern per model was never enough: the wavenumber, the phase per metre, the delay phase and the crossover frequency were all taken from one scene-wide value, so moving the Q21S's dropdown re-drew the Q212P's interference. Measured on a two-device plan, retuning one device moved the other's field by up to 18.3 dB; it is now 0.000 dB. Speakers that share a frequency still interfere and are summed as complex pressure; speakers at different frequencies cannot interfere, so their energies add instead, and a scene at one frequency solves exactly as before. The relative heatmap's normalisation was a second coupling of the same kind - one scene-wide unity-gain peak meant retuning the Q212P moved the Q21S's colours by about 3 dB although its field never moved - so each frequency is now normalised by its own peak, in the map, the pressure view, the coherence ratio and the Directivity polar. Covered by a new verification suite of 297,806 checks over every frequency of every model pair, which the previous engine fails 2,374 of. Also fixed: the Q212P's chosen frequency was never remembered (its slot was missing from the per-model memory, so it reverted to 484 Hz whenever another model was browsed) and each model's frequency is now saved in the project; a Q212P frequency-response sweep moved the sub's frequency instead of its own; and the Q212P raw-data fallback path was mis-escaped. The Mapping ribbon follows the Figma: Options is split into Ortho (the mode) and Ortho Controls (the things it switches on), Plane is named Plane Prediction, the Ortho controls sit on one row of glyphs with the caption underneath instead of being split across two rows, the linked-spacing control is a boxed read-out rather than a slider, and every cluster is centred on its plate - the glyphs used to start at the plate's left edge while the caption centred, leaving dead space on the right of any cluster with a long caption.

The Q212P joins the Q21S and the BEM 2inch as a cabinet you can place. Pick it in the cabinet list and the frequency catalogue switches to its six measured bands - 484, 1088, 2078, 3969, 8909 and 17013 Hz - taken from the supplied BEM field export of 41,185 points over a 10 m forward hemisphere. Units name themselves Q212P_1, Q212P_2 and carry an aiming ray, as a top should. Polars are published at 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 m and embedded in the binary, so the model works from a portable copy with no data folder beside it. Two caveats travel with the set: the export mesh covers the front hemisphere only, so the rear is synthesised by holding the 90 degree value and readings behind a Q212P are a floor rather than a measurement; and no sensitivity figure was supplied, so the set is relative dB like the horn - coverage and directivity are right, absolute SPL is not claimed. Cabinet size, 400 x 700 x 450 mm, is provisional until a spec sheet arrives. Show Values is now a probe rather than a grid: arming it turns the cursor into a crosshair and reads the SPL at whatever point it hovers, so a value can be taken anywhere on the map instead of only where a label fits. Fixes: subs no longer answer Show Rays, since a Q21S is aimed with the right-click rotation handle and rays are for mids and tops; the 'is this a subwoofer' test was written backwards as 'is not the horn', which would have filed every model added after it - the Q212P first - as a sub and taken its ray away; CSV exports count each cabinet in their own right instead of heading a Q212P-only scene Product,Q21S(1); and the Q212P absolute raw-data fallback path was mis-escaped, so the last-resort folder never resolved.

First archived build under the Atomik Integral name. The Mapping ribbon is drawn from the Figma icon set - Show Rays, Lock Rays, SPL Mapping / Mapping Off, Show Interdistance, Show Values, Snap, Ortho with its Horizontal / Vertical / Gap, then Use as Plane, Virtual, Architectural, Listening, Seated, Standing, Mic, + Range and Show / Hide ranges - in three states: grey when unavailable, black when available and off, red when on. Hovering shows the name the button used to carry, in bold, over its description. The Mapping icons are a third larger, and the status message moved into the tab strip so it shows in full instead of being cut to 'Project...'. The mic X / Y boxes name their axis inside the field. The mouse wheel now sets numbers: hover over any sidebar number box - position, gain, delay, rotation, height, tilt, crossover, band top, resolution, floor, layout - or the mic X / Y and the wheel steps it, Shift for ten; elsewhere it still scrolls the panel. New shapes are light blue #A9C7FF at 100% opacity instead of yellow at 35%. Carries v1.4.3, which had no archive build: renamed Atomik Integral; mics placed by typing X / Y; Show Values as a live crosshair probe; magnifier rebuilt; readability pass; Show Rays for mids and tops only.

The crossover now reaches every view: it was applied inside the smoothed band sum the SPL map is built from and nowhere else, leaving the single-frequency pressure field, the incoherent sum and the Directivity polar drawn from the unfiltered signal. It is also taken at the frequency actually being propagated rather than the browsed model's own catalogue frequency, which only matched in a single-model scene. Both frequency-response displays now read calibrated dB SPL on an axis anchored when the first curve arrives, instead of a map-relative figure on a scale that re-centred on every solve - so a filter, a gain or a delay is visible as a change in level. The Listen window's probe was running with no directivity tables and no calibration and now gets the real ones. The view no longer snaps back to the same framing after every edit. Subs carry no aiming ray, as ArrayCalc and EASE Focus steer low end by array geometry and delay rather than by pointing a cabinet. Added: each mic prints its X, Y beside its marker in the unit on show, with a Show Coordinates toggle; right-click the plot to copy the canvas to the clipboard at 2x, caption included, ready to paste anywhere. The Frequency Response window is laid out from its own size - the dB span fits the data, gridlines and ticks thin themselves, the legend steps aside when narrow - and the crossover row labels scale like every other sidebar label.

Crossover filters on any cabinet. Select a speaker and choose Off / Low pass / High pass, Linkwitz-Riley or Butterworth, 2nd or 4th order, at a corner you set; the settings apply to the whole selection and save with the project. The transfer functions are the analogue prototypes evaluated at the run frequency, verified against the reference implementation over 288 combinations with a largest difference of 0.000e+00. H is applied to the complex pressure, so a crossover moves phase as well as level and therefore moves where cabinets sum and cancel, and it is evaluated at every smoothing sub-band rather than once at the band centre. Ranges can be hidden without being forgotten. Fixes: mics snapped to a hard-coded 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 m ring set that was drawn nowhere; Place on ring now offers the ranges you actually added. Previously numbered 1.5.0 - same build, renumbered to keep the line on 1.4.x; this EXE still reports 1.5.0 in its own file properties.

Home / Mapping ribbon tabs. Aiming rays out of every speaker, grabbable anywhere along their length to turn it, with Lock Rays and whole-selection turning. Any shape can be marked a Listening, Virtual or Architectural plane, each with its own stroke: Listening and Architectural planes stop a ray, a Virtual plane lets it through, and a Listening plane clips the SPL map to the audience and reports coverage from the solved grid on its tag. Listening height (Seated 1.2 m / Standing 1.7 m) documents a plane and deliberately does not feed the prediction. Show Values prints the predicted level across the map. Range rings at any distance you type, metric or imperial, with chips to delete them. Listen at a mic: a track or pink noise filtered to what the engine predicts at that point, following the mic as you drag it. Rectangles and squares rotate. A second click reaches the shape underneath. Fixes: text boxes keep their font and colour when edited, rotate with their box and measure in line boxes; Frequency Response no longer flat with one mic; deleting a mic or closing the Listen window stops the audio; the ribbon no longer runs over the Ready pill; MP3 loads (the build had no audio backends compiled in at all).

Speakers can be aimed: selected units show a handle off their front face that turns the cabinet in 5-degree steps, with the live angle beside the knob. The heading is saved per speaker (older projects open pointing +x as before) and is a real change of firing direction, so rotating re-solves the field. Plan footprints now follow the placement sketch - Q21S 900 x 1000 mm, BEM 2inch 500 x 500 mm - with heights unchanged; the engine's near-field floor follows the new depths (Q21S 512 -> 500 mm, horn 75 -> 250 mm), so levels right beside a cabinet move slightly while the far field does not. A Show sizes checkbox dimensions every cabinet on the plan (W along the baffle, D along the firing axis, H called out as vertical), and Speaker Properties gains View in 3D: the cabinet as a draggable solid with a red baffle and W / H / D marked on its own edges. All non-ASCII text removed from the UI, fixing the mojibake in the Properties dialog and two tooltips. Elevation views, per-speaker height / tilt and Z / F shortcuts are built but hidden behind a flag. Q21S, BEM 2inch and UI assets embedded.

Export sheet metrics redesigned: the charcoal strip carrying a second wordmark and a run-on line of facts is replaced by a labelled key/value panel in the same language as the project block - Frequency, Wavelength, Devices, Directivity, Scale, Dynamic range, Grid - with a plain sign-off line beneath. Peak SPL is withdrawn from the PNG sheet and the PDF report: absolute calibration was being inferred from a bare magnitude test, so the 2" horn's unit-drive BEM data was printed as real SPL beside Q21S as if the two were comparable; it is now declared per source and can be switched back on once the horn's sensitivity is known. Selecting a speaker model or a placed unit no longer re-solves the scene - the scene carries its own frequency, seeded from the first unit placed and changed only by an explicit pick in the Frequency dropdown; selecting a unit repoints that dropdown to the unit's own model for reference. Adding a unit still re-solves. Corrects the Q21S cabinet, whose width and height were swapped against the manufacturer's W x H x D = 1546 x 679 x 1024 mm, so its plan footprint was drawn at under half its true width. Each model now carries its own cabinet: the 2" horn is 459 x 276.5 x 150 mm against the Q21S's 1546 x 679 x 1024 mm, so its plan marker is drawn to scale and the engine's near-field floor is per-speaker rather than one Q21S-derived constant. Fixes exports silently not overwriting (the PNG sheet and SPL CSV were appended to an existing file, so the previous content kept showing while the timestamp updated), the unit dropdown wrapping onto two lines for longer model names, and mis-encoded separators in exported text (/utf-8 added to both build configs).

BEM 2inch added as a second speaker model alongside Q21S. A Speaker model picker chooses what new units are created as, and every unit carries its own model tag, so one scene can mix both and each unit is simulated from its own model's measured data - the two are never blended. The horn brings its own 9-band frequency catalogue (64 - 17266 Hz) and its own embedded polar pack. Unit names now use a space-free model tag numbered within their own model, so a BEM unit placed second overall reads BEM2inch_1. The redundant Measurement set row is gone. Note: this BEM run is unit-drive normalised, so absolute levels are not yet comparable with Q21S in a mixed scene. Q21S, BEM 2inch and UI assets embedded in the EXE.

New Rel. SPL gradient from the Figma colour picker: #FF0103 -> #F65556 -> #CD617C -> #3281B9 -> #003A6C -> #151515, replacing the previous seven-stop ramp. The stop positions are deliberately uneven - red holds to 30% and the crossover is at 47% - giving a longer hot band. Legend tick labels 18% larger. Q21S and UI assets embedded in the EXE.

Q21S units capped at 8. SPL solve runs on all cores (0.4s -> 0.1s for 8 units at 400 Hz). Autosave timing and status corrected - it could previously sit unsaved for up to 45 s, and edits never showed as unsaved at all. Opacity percentage now tracks the slider, is larger, and greys out when there is no fill to change. Grey sidebar outlines, larger field labels, bigger Recent Projects list. Q21S and UI assets embedded in the EXE. Sidebar section titles in sentence case and larger Rel. SPL legend tick labels.

Plot never letterboxes: the fill-the-canvas fit is the zoom floor, so there are no margins at any zoom, with the field still 100 x 100 m and grid cells square. Pan fixed and middle-drag pans from any tool. Q21S cabinet corrected to its real 1546 x 679 x 1024 mm and drawn to scale against the grid. SPL caption back at the canvas edge. Q21S and UI assets embedded in the EXE. Lighter grid lines so the metre grid no longer overpowers the SPL field (major 42%, minor 16% alpha).

Figma UI cut: new ATOMIK. wordmark, tool ribbon, sidebar and dashboard built to measured Figma geometry. Heatmap renamed Gradient Plot. Square grid cells ruled edge to edge with no dead margins. Contrast-aware axis numbers and canvas caption. Sidebar holds its width share at any aspect ratio; 4K scale ceiling raised. Icon-free info panels with a close cross. Light theme only. Q21S still embedded. Assets (logos, ribbon icons, fonts) are now baked into the EXE, so a downloaded binary is self-contained.
Command registry (short=full name). Typed-point DRAW. MOVE/ZOOM sessions. Dock/undock terminal. Atomik HELP. Esc keeps floating terminal focused. Q21S still embedded.

Gain slider affects SPL again. Sidebar Delete removes all selected speakers. Text box annotations (fill + rotate). Clean slate on first open. Range off by default. Esc/Line/Shape-menu fixes. Command terminal (cls/clear). Delay max 10 ms. Q21S still embedded.
Mic ring snap restored (original Drag::Mic). Snap tak when drawings meet edge-to-edge. start.md. Q21S still embedded.
Mic receivers, FR window, Show Degrees, embedded Q21S (no Excel). Windows download is the Setup installer (EXE + fonts).
Baseline Q21S heatmap. Windows download is a ZIP (EXE + MeasurementIntegrationPack) so SPL works on any PC.
